metric_rationale: This metric isolates the specific trials where Take The Best (TTB) and Tallying make strictly opposite predictions (e.g., when one option wins on the single highest-validity cue, but the other option wins on a simple majority of all other cues). By computing the proportion of choices that align with TTB on these critical trials, the metric will yield values close to 1.0 if TTB is the true generating model, and values close to 0.0 if Tallying is the true generating model. The large and consistent gap between these outcomes perfectly discriminates the two theories.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic on trials where Tallying and Take The Best (TTB) make strictly opposite predictions. By isolating the exact trials where the highest-validity discriminating cue opposes the sheer number of winning features, the metric will yield a value close to 1 if the data is generated by Tallying and close to 0 if generated by TTB, providing maximal discrimination between the two models.

This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice aligns with the first discriminating cue (the highest validity cue that differs between the two options). Take The Best strictly follows this cue, so its simulated data will have a value near 1.0 (subject to noise). In contrast, the Weighted Additive model integrates all cues, and since the experimental design explicitly pits the first discriminating cue against multiple lower-validity cues, WADD will frequently choose the option favored by the compensatory cues, resulting in a significantly lower score.

Isolates trials where Option A has only 1 positive feature but it is the highest validity discriminating cue (Trials 1 and 2), while Option B has 3 or 4 lower-validity positive features. Take The Best (TTB) will almost exclusively choose A (response 0) because it stops at the first discriminating cue. Weighted Additive (WADD) will integrate the numerous lower-validity cues and frequently choose B (response 1), particularly for lower values of the gamma parameter. Thus, the proportion of B choices on these specific trials strongly discriminates the theories.

Previous metrics failed because the parameter distributions (gamma for WADD, theta for Bounded Threshold) cause both models to behave identically to Take-The-Best for ~90% of subjects, while the remaining ~10% exhibit opposing behavior on conflict trials. This creates massive bimodal variance that destroys statistical significance. To bypass this, we measure TTB adherence strictly on the 'consensus' trials (T6 and T4) where BOTH models theoretically predict a 100% win rate for the TTB option across all parameter values (for WADD, 0.95^g + 0.85^g > 0.75^g + 0.65^g for all g>0). This completely eliminates the bimodal strategy variance, leaving only the noise parameters. Since WADD is parametrized with a much higher lapse rate (epsilon up to 0.5) than Bounded Threshold (epsilon up to 0.1), WADD will exhibit a significantly lower adherence on these consensus trials, and the drastically reduced variance will make this gap highly significant.

Measures the proportion of times the subject chooses the 'moderate' option (the one lacking the single highest validity cue) on trials where the linear sum of validities is perfectly tied. Theory 2 (Evidence Accumulation) either stops early and picks the extreme option, or integrates all cues and predicts a tie (50% max for the moderate option). Theory 1 (WADD with exponent) can systematically prefer the moderate option if gamma < 1, leading to a higher choice rate for the moderate option.
